claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density near 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa near 1000 °C.
Replacing about 20–30% of the Hf content with Al will reduce the alloy density by at least approximately 10%.
Replacing about 20–30% of the Hf content with Al will preserve room-temperature yield strength within approximately 10% of the HfMoTaTiZr baseline.
Replacing about 20–30% of the Hf content with Al will preserve yield strength near 1000 °C within approximately 10% of the HfMoTaTiZr baseline.
The Al-substituted HfMoTaTiZr alloy will retain a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution.
Controlled Al addition will moderate lattice distortion in the BCC solid solution.
Al is much lighter than Hf, so replacing Hf with Al decreases average atomic mass and alloy density.
Al incorporated into the BCC lattice will maintain solid-solution strengthening through controlled lattice distortions.
Simultaneously reducing density by at least 10% and retaining yield strength within 10% will enhance specific strength.
There is an Al-substitution threshold below which secondary-phase formation and significant microstructural degradation can be avoided.

contradictions.description: The conditions permit optionally homogenized samples, whereas the experimental design calls for all alloys to use the same as-cast processing route. Including homogenized specimens would change the processing state and weaken the controlled comparison unless they are treated as a separate experimental arm.
